title: Experience Friction Detector
outcome: Find confusing steps, excessive waiting, repeated actions, and hidden dead ends
breakthrough: The platform continuously removes user effort
lane: Completion, review, quality, and user-outcome validation

phases.name: Phase 1 - Build the Experience Friction Detector Core

subphases.name: 1.1 Experience Friction Detector Domain Model and State Plane
work: Define typed entities, capabilities, jobs, events, state transitions, and outputs required to find confusing steps, excessive waiting, repeated actions, and hidden dead ends, with explicit versions and validation at every boundary.

Implement an owned persistent state layer optimized for completion confidence, functional review, usability, friction, release quality, and outcome prediction; include snapshots or event history when state changes over time.
Expose create, query, update, subscribe, and delete operations through local APIs plus an SDK that never requires private cross-runtime imports.

subphases.name: 1.2 Experience Friction Detector Execution Runtime
work: Build resumable workers and state machines that perform the core operation: find confusing steps, excessive waiting, repeated actions, and hidden dead ends.
Add cancellation, idempotency, bounded retries, timeouts, quotas, sandbox limits, and deterministic recovery from partial failure.
Create a local simulator that can replay success, malformed inputs, disconnection, overload, provider loss, and restart recovery.

phases.name: Phase 2 - Make Experience Friction Detector Adaptive and Usable

subphases.name: 2.1 Experience Friction Detector Decision and Learning Engine
work: Implement scoring, planning, prediction, search, or optimization using risk scoring, behavioral simulation, anomaly detection, acceptance modeling, and experience analytics.
Create feedback signals from task outcomes and user corrections; update tunable behavior without silently changing hard safety limits.
Return confidence, alternatives, bottlenecks, and a concise machine-readable explanation for every important automated choice.

subphases.name: 2.2 Experience Friction Detector Interaction Surface
work: Build the primary experience in the completion radar, review arena, friction heatmap, and release confidence view, including live state, controls, errors, and recovery actions.
Add a CLI and typed client library so humans, agents, games, and third-party applications can operate the capability directly.
Stream progress and intermediate artifacts in real time so long operations remain inspectable, interruptible, and steerable.

phases.name: Phase 3 - Scale Experience Friction Detector into a Breakthrough Product

subphases.name: 3.1 Experience Friction Detector Offline, Edge, and Cloud Mesh
work: Implement local-only, hybrid, and cloud execution with explicit capability discovery and graceful behavior when optional peers disappear.
Add conflict-safe synchronization, workload placement, caching, backpressure, and failover across devices or nodes where the feature benefits from distribution.
Benchmark latency, throughput, memory, energy, network transfer, and cost; make the scheduler choose the best execution mode from measured constraints.

subphases.name: 3.2 Experience Friction Detector Signature Breakthrough
work: Implement the differentiating behavior: The platform continuously removes user effort. Ship it as an opt-in executable mode, not a mockup.
Run adversarial, load, privacy, misuse, degraded-network, and recovery tests against the novel behavior; block unsafe automatic actions.
Package the feature as an independently installable capability with a live demo, sample integration, metrics endpoint, and rollback-safe release artifact.
